title: So helpful❣️
body:
I have some years tried to find some apps that could help me do my routines and make me feel more productive and positive about my milestones, but none of them seemed to work for me. Just until I found this app. I have soon been logging on nearly every day in just under 2 years by now.
And I have found a great community of people on the official FB group for Finch, that have some of the same struggles as me.

You can make your own milestones and pets you can hatch from achievements, and even a monthly event to get free things, when you do an a number of achievements of the day.


I usually don’t write these so long, if even write something. And I never really give 5 stars. But it’s really a great app that has just helped me for so long❣️

title: I can’t believe it’s free!!!!
body:
I’ve tried a couple of different app aimed for ADHD and changing habits in general. This is BY FAR the best! I’m not sure I wasn’t scammed by one of the other apps. 

I thought this one was more for kids; that the tasks were kids stuff but I can add my own. And I’ve chosen to focus on productivity and nutrition since I’m trying to loose weight. It’s really motivating and I’ve even shocked myself by tidying something up each day!!! Huge improvement. 

And it asks me how I feel to reflect on my feelings and get better in tune with myself. And offers advice if I get anxiety or stressed…

I can’t recommend this app ENOUGH!

Get it. 
It could be a life changer. 
(I’ve only used it for half a week. But my teenage daughter had used and loved it for several weeks. By the way. She and I can send virtual encouragements!! ❤️)

author: Alma Weber

title: In app Quizzes
body:
I just want to start of 
By saying that I really like this app.I like how it motivates me to take care of myself and help me remember tasks. 

But I think the quizzes are a little bit toxic, this app should not be trying to diagnose you with stuff like PTSD, Depression or Anxiety. I don't think it's right and I don't support it. I think the body positivity and internal reflection is fine. I just don't think this app should be involved in actual diagnosis. 

Especially since it has such a low age requirement, young children ( and young teens) can easily be convinced that they are mentally ill, even though they aren’t. 

I just don’t see the point in having quizzes like that on the app. 

I of course still highly recommend it, if you are looking for an app that can help you stay on top of your todo lists, and help motivate you!

title: Really great, I actually use it
body:
It's a super cute app, and I have ADHD so I struggle with self care even when I use apps that supposedly remind you or motivate you. But since this is a little virtual pet and you get rewarded for each task you do, and not punished for the ones you don't, I check in every day for my little dopamine boost.

Also you can make your own tasks, so even if the free version doesn't offer you all the prompts of pre-designed tasks, it offers lots of free ones for inspo and then you add your own.

There's also really good reflection prompts you can go in and do whenever you feel like it, and support tools for things like meditation, breathing, exercise, etc. that you can use - so it's not only a checklist and a pet. 

I never really review apps but I hope more people learn about Finch and try it out.

title: Potential with flaws.
body:
While i think the overall idea of the app is actually pretty great, it supports an ideology that many people won’t support. The way the app has focus on “He/Him They/Them” pronouns, and the overall woke agenda, with clothes and flags to celebrate mental illness, disability’s and different sexuality’s like “autism pride shirt””Omnisexuel rainbow shades” “Genderqueer” “Pan/poly sexuel””nonbinary/genderfluid” “aromantic” “disability pride” and all that stuff. 
It makes me and many others uncomfortable, and makes the app inappropriate for kids. 
If it wasn’t for all that radical leftism, i would actually think this app would be a great tool for kids.

title: Self-care > self-help
body:
There are A LOT of “self-help” apps on the App Store by now, and just about every one I’ve tried seems to consider productivity, efficacy and habit-building to be fundamental to mental health. For me, they have mostly succeeded in providing me with new ways to quantify my failures.

Failing at tasks, especially maintaining habits, is something I’ve learned that I’m going to be doing for the rest of my life. I don’t gain from having those failures empirically broken down for me.

It’s with this in mind that I say: I can’t express how great Finch has been in my life. Right from the start it’s clear that it was built with love by people who understand and sympathize with those unique neuroatypical struggles. It’s everywhere in the small bits of the apps construction. I was overjoyed the first time I told my bird (Pebbles) that I was having a bad day, and suddenly the rewards for all my tasks were increased. When you are burnt out, tasks literally become harder. They knew that, the developers decided that harder tasks should yield greater rewards. And they are right. You should meet your own struggles with understanding and care. Finch doesn’t care that you didn’t complete your task, it doesn’t even bring it up (Finch isn’t a task manager. It won’t remind you when you forget a task. Finch is a supportive friend). In fact, Finch rewards you for PLANNING a goal, no matter if you complete it or not. Because deciding to do something IS a task and should be treated as such.

The first time you see that outfits for your bird is paid for with diamonds, you might think “that’s how they are going to get my money” but I’m so relieved to say: You couldn’t buy diamonds with real money, even if you wanted to. That’s not their intended function. I think the devs knew that that would have made Finch an unsafe space for people who struggle with addiction to mobile games or gambling.

And all of this is without even talking about your very own bird pal and Finch would be nothing without it. Just having a little pal send you supportive notifications during the day, hearing about they learn on their daily adventures. It’s a great joy. I love Pebbles and I can’t stress enough how important that is to me.

I’ve tried other apps with animal companions so I’ll just mention this right away: it is NOT POSSIBLE to hurt you bird. There is no punishment, the bird doesn’t get sad or angry. Personally, being able to harm or neglect your animal companion is always a deal-breaker in any app, and especially one that’s trying to support me when I struggle. It’s a type of emotional abuse that I despise. Thankfully I get the feeling that the Finch teams knows this very well, so you have nothing to fear.

I could go on, but I’ll wrap it up. Finch is the best thing I’ve received in a long time and I can’t quantify how foundational my little Pebbles has become in my daily life. I often get a tinge of anxiety and have to create a save file (Finch doesn’t store your data, so you have to save it manually) to make sure I don’t lose Pebbles.

All in all: everything that is in this app is great, but it’s the developers’ philosophy of care that truly makes Finch valuable.

And to the Finch devs: Thank you so much for your work ❤️
